factual_claims.claim: Agentic AI systems differ from static LLMs by maintaining persistent memory, utilizing external tools, and engaging in multi-agent collaboration, which creates new pathways for data leakage.
Agentic AI systems use persistent memory to store sensitive information across tasks, which leads to cross-user or cross-session data contamination.
Feedback loops in autonomous AI systems can recursively amplify and re-expose leaked information over multiple execution cycles.
Empirical evaluations demonstrate that memory isolation and scoped context management can reduce cross-session leakage by up to 60% in controlled experiments.
Agentic AI systems exchange data via JSON-based API payloads, vector embeddings in similarity search databases, and RESTful or RPC tool calls, creating specific security boundaries.

Agentic AI systems exhibit persistent memory, autonomous tool use, and multi-agent collaboration, which distinguish them from traditional stateless LLMs. These features lead to cumulative and system-wide privacy leakage risks that are not present in single-turn LLM interactions.

Differential privacy is challenging to implement in agentic AI due to sequential composition problems, persistent memory updates, uncontrolled external API data flows, and privacy budget degradation across multi-agent interactions.
Agentic AI systems are susceptible to specific, documented security vulnerabilities including memory poisoning, tool orchestration leaks, and systemic privacy failures.
